anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific typed-array value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after staged UI gating, custom-event dispatch, action routing, tuple preparation and asynchronous continuation, whose own body constructs the target observable typed_array_payload value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging a return value, or emitting it to the console.

primary_anchor.source_export: private helper reached through exported u(config)
primary_anchor.why: First target-specific value-construction function: it normalizes the staged table tuple into source text, materializes the target Uint8Array through its helpers, and returns the observable ta_ typed_array_payload string.
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only: the canonical anchor answer is captured_span plus answer_function as declared in the captured bundle slice. source_function is a private maintainer mapping into src/.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle (hash/offset/complete function body). Agents only see captures, so the standard answer identifier is primary_anchor.answer_function, not source_function.

A returned function name is scored against answer_function in the captured corpus. source_function is a private maintainer label and is not something an agent can know unless the bundle still exposes that exact identifier.

Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from staged button handlers, custom-event dispatch, action routing, input preparation, tuple normalization, byte materialization, encoding helper, factory wrapper, sink and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.

role_oracle.why: First target-specific value-construction function: it normalizes the staged table tuple into source text, materializes the target Uint8Array through its helpers, and returns the observable ta_ typed_array_payload string.
Materializes the 18-byte Uint8Array that carries the transformed tuple lanes, transit values, priority and review-sensitive statistics consumed by the payload encoder.
Serializes the transformed Uint8Array into the ta_ base64url typed_array_payload string observed in the console object.
Computes the per-lane 32-bit words that feed the target Uint8Array materialization helper.
Normalizes the ordered tuple fields, transit and statistics context into the source text consumed by the typed-array lane transformation.
Generic tuple-to-map conversion utility used before source text and byte-array construction.
Generic 32-bit rotate utility used by the lane mixing and context folding helpers.
Generic final integer mixer used below the lane transformation and not itself the target constructor.
Exported factory that closes over the slot config and returns the per-slot reducer that calls the anchor; it does not itself materialize the Uint8Array or encode the payload.
Installs the delegated click listener and the commit CustomEvent listener, enforcing the arm, preview and commit sequence before routing the committed snapshot into the transformation chain.
Checks staged arm and preview readiness and dispatches the commit CustomEvent with the form snapshot, but does not build the typed-array payload.
Builds the console object around an already constructed typed_array_payload value and the table segment metadata; it does not construct the value.
Console sink that freezes and logs the already constructed typed_array_payload object with console.log; it should not outrank the constructor anchor.
Updates the visible table state around the same flow but does not construct the target typed-array payload.
Maintains shadow cache values for diversion checks and does not feed the target console field.
Emits preview.shadow / table.shadow.action diversion output and is explicitly outside the requested table.segment.commit typed_array_payload target.

scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: Staged button handlers, custom-event dispatch, action routing, tuple preparation and table painting are required path gates but do not construct typed_array_payload.
The exported factory only wraps the private typed-array anchor and should not outrank the anchor itself.
The final console sink and payload wrappers emit an already constructed typed_array_payload value.
The shadow table action path can emit debug objects during interaction but does not carry typed_array_payload under table.segment.commit.
The target value is deterministic for the same controls and sensitive to status, minimum amount, owner, priority and review-mode changes.
debug_hints_private: The primary anchor is visible in the captured bundle as function transformTableTypedArray(...).
The target field name typed_array_payload is reassembled at the sink from character-code arrays.
The byte materialization helper contains new Uint8Array(18).
The page path requires Arm, Preview and Commit before the target CustomEvent routes into the transformation chain.
Source paths are private evaluator mapping aids, not the default public answer space.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Returned span maps uniquely to the captured transformTableTypedArray anchor function.
Returned span maps to a target-specific helper below the anchor, such as materializeLaneBytes, encodeTypedArrayPayload or laneWord.
Returned span maps to a generic utility directly used by the typed-array transformation path, such as createSource, mapRows, rot or fmix.
Returned span maps to a path-critical routing/gating function, the factory wrapper, or a payload/sink wrapper that only emits an already constructed value.
Returned span maps to a generic DOM or tuple helper used in upstream preparation but absent from the detailed role oracle.
Returned span maps to an off-chain shadow decoy or cannot be uniquely mapped to a captured function.
